page: Amazon Web Services g6.xlarge is a graphics-intensive, GPU-accelerated server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. For acceleration, it includes a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with 22 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided via a 250 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance, as well as specialized GPU capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%, and average single-core performance in Geekbench and Passmark CPU tests. However, multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded decompression, and memory bandwidth fall into the bottom 25%. Despite these multi-core and memory throughput limitations, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in the top 10% for LLM inference, specifically in prompt processing and text generation for both small and medium models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g6.xlarge offers a specialized hardware profile that pairs an entry-level CPU configuration with a highly capable Ada Lovelace GPU and local NVMe storage. This resource density makes it highly cost-effective for workloads that can offload intensive computations to the GPU rather than relying on high multi-core CPU or memory bandwidth. Consequently, this instance is best suited for small to medium LLM inference, graphics-intensive applications, and GPU-accelerated machine learning tasks, whereas it is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded CPU compilation, high-throughput database operations, or high-bandwidth web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services g6.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server designed for graphics-intensive and machine learning workloads. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 250 GB local NVMe SSD. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with 22 GB of VRAM. While benchmarks indicate weak multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, the instance achieves top-tier results in LLM inference for small and medium models, alongside strong single-core CPU performance. This configuration offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-centric tasks by pairing a modest CPU allocation with a high-performance accelerator. It is highly suited for small-scale LLM deployment, machine learning inference, and graphics workloads, but less effective for CPU-heavy multi-threaded applications or high-throughput database operations.
